subject: Dedicated reservation options and activation schedule for Orbitum
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@orbitum.ai>, Procurement <procurement@orbitum.ai>
Cc: Marta Reyes <marta@orbitum.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation options and activation schedule for Orbitum

Hi Alex / team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — good discussion on forecasted peak hours and the latency targets you're trying to hit for the assistive search product. Per our follow-up, I put together three reservation structures that balance predictable baseline throughput with flexibility for burst/seasonal demand. Attached: orbitum-reserve-offer-v1.pdf and a quick activation workbook (gpu-activation-schedule.xlsx).

High-level options (summary):

1) Baseline + Burst (Conservative)
- Cluster: 8 x A100 equivalent nodes (64 vGPU units).
- Contract minimum: 40 GPUs reserved (guaranteed capacity).
- Burst pool: up to +30% on pay-as-you-go rates during defined surge windows.
- Ramp: 6-week onramp to reach baseline, with 2-week warmstart credits (50% discounted tokens during warmup).

2) Staircase Commitment (Recommended for predictable growth)
- Cluster: start 6 nodes, step to 10 nodes over 3 quarters.
- Contract minimums: 30 GPUs first 90 days, 50 GPUs after quarter 2.
- Activation windows: monthly pre-warm + auto-scale policy for synthetic load testing.
- Credits: 1 week of prewarmed reserved capacity per tranche.

3) Flexible Slate (Max flexibility)
- Cluster: virtualized pool, min 20 GPUs with soft floor (best-effort guarantees).
- Burst: large burst allowance (subject to availability) with fallbacks to smaller model variants.
- Ramp: immediate activation for 20 GPUs, optional rapid step-ups within 48 hours for new spikes.

Questions for your procurement / infra:
- Do you need a hard minimum (true SLA-backed GPU count) or is a soft floor acceptable?
- Any blackout windows for upgrades or warmups (night/weekend)?
- Preferred billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly)?

Requested next steps:
- Let us know which option most closely matches Orbitum's risk profile. If you want, we can model expected token burn and per-token cost across the staircase option (we find it helpful for finance).

I'm looping in our deployment leads internally to confirm warmstart feasibility and the timing assumptions.

Thanks,

Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Sean — thanks, this is helpful. A few quick clarifications before we run this by finance/infra: 

- For the Staircase Commitment (recommended), can you confirm whether the step from 6 -> 10 nodes requires lead time for provisioning (we have planned product launches each quarter)?
- The warmstart credits — are those applied as monthly invoice credits or as upfront credits against committed spend?
- On the Flexible Slate: curious how fallbacks to smaller model variants will affect latency in the 95th percentile. Can you point to any observed latency deltas (p90/p95) when degrading model size?

Procurement: when you have a moment, what internal approvals do you need to sign off on a staircase structure with quarterly step-ups?

Appreciate the quick answers — Alex

Sean / team,

Quick answers — apologies for the brief note, this is actionable: 

1) Provisioning lead time: for A100-equivalent nodes in Dedicated pools we typically need 10 business days to guarantee physical capacity if they want guaranteed racks. If Orbitum is OK with scheduler-priority within a dedicated cluster (soft isolation), we can do the 6->10 step within 48 hours most of the time. For contract language, call out whether the step requires "physical activation" (10 business days) vs "logical allocation" (48 hours).

2) Warmstart credits: standard is one-time onboarding credit applied as a deduction against the first two monthly invoices (we do pro-rata if onboarding spans billing periods). We can also structure as committed credit on the first invoice if finance prefers it communicated upfront.

3) Latency deltas on fallback: based on recent telemetry (MedTech customer case):
- Model rdx-large -> rdx-medium: p50 +5ms, p90 +28ms, p95 +42ms (longer sequences amplify the delta).
- Embeddings: switching to quantized-medium variants increased p95 by ~30ms but reduced cost by ~35%.

Proposal for response back to Orbitum: recommend the Staircase Commitment (option 2) with this contract language: 
- Step-up clause: logical allocation within 48 hours for the first two tranches, physical activation (10 business days) only for final +4 node increments that exceed pool capacity.
- Warmstart credits: one-time onboarding credit applied to first two invoices (explicit $ amount in SOW).
- Safety fallback: fall back to rdx-medium automatically if p95 latency breaches 600ms for >5 consecutive minutes; traffic will be re-routed to fallback with a post-incident analysis.

I'll attach the short SOW text and approximate pricing lines — Irene, can you add the SOW snippet and the exact credit amount to the document before Sean sends?

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Director, Dedicated Services | Redwood Inference
